title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 8: goodness wills some good to each — not equal goods by foresight
pass_a_gloss: Solution. From this, that God is good by nature, it is rightly inferred that he wills good to every creature of his; but not rightly, that he wills any and every good to any and every creature, or equal and the same goods to equal creatures. Nor even in dispensing the goods falsely called of Nature or of Fortune is God bound either to dispense these from a foreseen good use of them, or to impart them to the greater part of human beings. For we see that neither strength of body, nor sharpness of mind, nor beauty of form, nor abundance of riches is given from foresight of good use. For, for the most part, they are given to those who abuse all these things most badly, unto injury, unto fraud, unto lust, unto luxury. Yet these very goods themselves are granted only to few.
pass_b_english: Sol. From God's being good by nature it rightly follows that he wills some good to every creature of his — not that he wills every good to every creature, or the same equal goods to equal creatures. Even in dispensing so-called goods of Nature or Fortune he is not bound to give them from foresight of good use, nor to impart them to the majority. We see strength of body, sharpness of mind, beauty of form, and abundance of riches are not given from foresight of good use — for the most part they go to those who abuse them worst: to injury, fraud, lust, luxury. And even those goods are granted only to few.
source_text: Sol. Ex eo quod Deus sit natura bonus, recte infertur, illum velle bonum omni suae creaturae; sed non recte, illum velle quodvis bonum cuivis creaturae, aut aequalia et eadem bona aequalibus creaturis. Nec in Naturae quidem aut Fortunae falso dictis bonis dispensandis tenetur Deus aut haec dispensare ex praeviso bono usu eorum, aut ea majori parti hominum impertire. Videmus siquidem neque robur corporis, neque acumen mentis, neque formae venustatem, neque divitiarum affluentiam dari ex boni usus praescientia. Nam, ut plurimum, dantur illis, qui hisce omnibus pessime abutuntur, ad injuriam, ad fraudem, ad libidinem, ad luxuriam. Haec tamen ipsa bona non nisi paucis conceduntur.
